question: Was the OCFDA geometry/competitive result specific to Llama-3.2-1B?
scope_notes: Only the host model changes relative to the completed 1B competitive gate.
Task, training snapshot, held-out suite (805 examples), validation split, evaluator, and generation settings transfer unchanged.
No LR search: all three methods use the transferred 5e-4 selected in setting 1.
Nine full trainings: 3 methods x 3 matched configurations; no selection phase.

budget.ocfda_k_selection_rule: integer k minimizing |3*layers*k*hidden - reference_lora_params|; k=47 frozen
budget.super_budget_rule: same rank-equivalent sparse policy as setting 1: Wanda-BottomK mask sized by reference_lora_params/target_dense_params per matrix
budget.budget_source: arithmetic from the frozen architecture block; cross-checked against AutoConfig on the run host

interpretation.geometry_transfer: PASS (descriptive) if aligned mean > independent mean AND aligned wins >= 2/3 matched configurations; 3/3 is strong replication. FAIL otherwise.
interpretation.competitiveness: PASS if aligned mean is within 2.0 pp of the Super-BottomK mean or better.
interpretation.independence: Two independent questions; 'geometry transfers, competitiveness does not' is a legitimate reported outcome, not a goalpost move.

resource_expectations.basis: extrapolated from 1B measured runs: train 393-451 s; eval wall 1270-1680 s; peak VRAM 21.4-24.0 GB; scaled by ~3x FLOPs and ~2.16x parameter count

provenance_notes: Baseline optimizer recipes match setting 1 (OCFDA AdamW/wd0, Super Adam/wd0 per the Super-Tuning paper).
Super calibration policy matches setting 1 (C4, 128 samples, seed 228, Wanda-BottomK).
The 3B checkpoint metadata protocol is B2-OCFDA; the 1B B1-OCFDA protocol is untouched.
